metas.name: Barren Highlands - Southwest
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Bright Colored Moss - Lillehammer and Oppdal
metas.note: Brightly coloured moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Coastal Grasslands - Far North
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Exposed Rock - South Coast
metas.note: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, are mainly found on the south coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: fjords - West Coast
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Northeast Landscape - Small Birches and Rolling Landscape
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Northern Scratches - Scratches on the road
metas.note:
In the north of the country (north of Narvik), it's very common to see these scratches on the road which are caused by snowmobiles in the area.

NOTE: These scratches can be somewhat difficult to find, so make sure to look closely if you suspect it's north.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Oslo Farmlands - Flat Landscape
metas.note: The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Pines - Coastal and Southern
metas.note: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Pteridium aquilinum/bracken - South
metas.note: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Sharp, Rocky mountains - Lofoten Archipelago
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Spruce - Southeast and Around Trondheim
metas.note: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Stavanger Farmlands - Rock Walls
metas.note: Similarly to the southeast, the farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. However, the fields look more vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Trondheim Farmlands - Very Hilly
metas.note: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.
